acceptance: Issue #3446 has a reply from the maintainer stating the decision.
If planned, a tracker item exists and is linked from the issue.
context:
Source: found on 2026-11-13 while delivering the agent-facing work (PRs BenchBox-dev/benchbox#4202, #4203 and BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site#152, #153, #154). The reply is the owner's; an agent may draft it from the issue and the platform registry. Guardrails: work in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight); never edit the primary clone. Related items share one feature branch and PR where their files overlap. No live-cloud runs and no credentials in Git or logs; heavy work only through lock-taking entry points or make heavy-run after make heavy-status. Follow the comment policy and add a changelog.d fragment for user-facing changes. Re-verify every cited file and line before acting; they are hints. Stop and report rather than widen scope.

Owner decision (2026-11-14): an agent drafts the reply into this item; the owner posts it under his own name. Nothing is posted by an agent.

Draft reply for the owner (2026-11-14), decision 'not planned for now, door left open':

Thanks for the request, and for the db-benchmark context — that is useful history.

I'm not planning to add data.table for now. Every platform BenchBox runs today is reached through a Python driver or library, and the timing, validation and result export all assume that. data.table would need a second runtime: R driven from Python through an R process or rpy2. The data crossing that boundary would be timed as part of the query, so the numbers wouldn't be comparable to the other DataFrame results, and CI and maintenance would have to carry R as well. I asked the question here because I couldn't find a bridge that keeps measurement honest, and your reply matches that.

You're right that this leaves out a tool that is still widely used and was the reference point for a lot of this field. If you or anyone else wants to take it on, the route I'd consider is a standalone R runner that executes the TPC-H-style queries natively, does its own timing, and writes a BenchBox result JSON for import. That would keep R outside the Python adapter layer, and I'd be glad to review it. If that would help, tell me what the result file would need to carry and I'll write it down.

I'm leaving the issue open as a record of the request, and I'll label it so it's clear it is a request, not in progress.

Before posting: the sentence about importing an external result JSON assumes an import path that was not verified; drop it if none exists. Alternative: ask 'Would a native R runner that emits a BenchBox result JSON meet your need?' and hold the decision.
description:
Problem: only three issues have ever come from outside contributors, and #3446 (a request about R data.table) is still open. The independent critique noted that real outside users ask for platforms and correctness, and an unanswered request costs more goodwill than any agent-facing feature gains.

Outcome: the issue gets a reply with a decision: planned with a tracker item, not planned with the reason, or a question back.
